title: Cell division
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.1.2-c04 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.2-c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.2-c12 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.1.2-c09 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Cell cycle
items.clue: The series of stages in which cells divide.

items.label: Gene
items.clue: A section of a DNA molecule carried on a chromosome.

items.label: Meristem tissue
items.clue: In plants, it can form any type of plant cell throughout life.

items.label: Stem cell
items.clue: Undifferentiated; it can divide many times and give rise to specialised types.

questions.stem: Which statement about chromosomes and genes in a body cell is correct?

options.text: A gene is made of a large number of chromosomes.
Each chromosome carries one gene made of DNA.
Each chromosome in the nucleus is found singly.
Each chromosome carries a large number of genes.

questions.explanation: The nucleus of a cell contains chromosomes made of DNA molecules, and each chromosome carries a large number of genes.

questions.stem: Which description gives the three overall stages of the cell cycle in the correct order?

options.text: The cell grows and copies its DNA, then the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm divides.
The nucleus divides first, then the cell grows and copies its DNA, then the cytoplasm divides.
The cell grows and halves its DNA, then the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm divides.
The cell grows and copies its DNA, then the nucleus divides, and division is complete.

questions.explanation: Before a cell can divide it grows and the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome; in mitosis one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides; finally the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.

questions.stem: How are the chromosomes normally arranged in a body cell?

options.text: Singly, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside a large gene in the cell.
In pairs, carrying a single gene per pair.

questions.explanation: In body cells the chromosomes are normally found in pairs, and the chromosomes are contained in the nucleus of the cell.

questions.stem: A human body cell containing 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. What does each new cell contain?

options.text: 23 chromosomes, identical to the parent cell
46 chromosomes, different from the parent cell
46 chromosomes, identical to the parent cell
23 chromosomes, different from the parent cell

questions.explanation: During the cell cycle the genetic material is doubled and then divided into two identical cells, so each new cell has the parent cell's 46 chromosomes.

questions.stem: Before a cell divides it grows and increases its number of ribosomes and mitochondria. What happens to the DNA at this stage?

options.text: The DNA is halved to leave one copy of each chromosome.
The DNA replicates after the nucleus has divided in two.
The DNA is altered so the two new cells are different.
The DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome.

questions.explanation: Before a cell can divide the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome, which is how the genetic material is doubled.

questions.stem: What happens during mitosis and the stage that follows it?

options.text: One set of chromosomes goes to each end, then the cytoplasm divides.
One set of chromosomes goes to each end, and the cell remains whole.
Half of each chromosome goes to each end, then the cytoplasm divides.
The chromosomes are shared unevenly, then the cytoplasm divides.

questions.explanation: In mitosis one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides; finally the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.

questions.stem: A cut on the arm of a fully grown adult heals as new skin cells are produced. Which statement about the new cells is correct?

options.text: New cells with half the chromosomes are made.
New identical cells are produced by mitosis.
New genetically different cells are produced.
Mitosis has stopped because the adult is grown.

questions.explanation: Cell division by mitosis produces two identical cells and is important in the growth and development of multicellular organisms, which includes producing new skin cells in this context.
